papers.title: Engineered broadband Purcell protection using a shared $Π$ filter for multiplexed superconducting qubits
papers.abstract: We propose a broadband Purcell-protection scheme based on a single shared filter integrated directly into the feedline, enabling simultaneous protection of multiple qubits in a compact architecture with minimal hardware overhead. The filter consists of two open-ended stubs connected by an in-line transmission line, forming a $Π$ geometry, and operates via engineered passive microwave interference that suppresses the real part of the environmental admittance over a wide frequency window. Circuit simulations and finite-element modeling show that transmission is suppressed by several orders of magnitude within the target band (the qubits' frequencies) while preserving the readout mode of the multiplexed architecture. For realistic device parameters, the proposed design yields Purcell-limited relaxation times exceeding $1$ ms over a frequency span of approximately $1.5$ GHz. Our results establish the $Π$ filter as a compact and scalable solution for broadband impedance engineering in superconducting quantum circuits, compatible with standard dispersive readout protocols.

similar_to.title: Broadband Purcell Filter for Fast Superconducting Qubit Reset and Readout
High-performance multiplexed readout of superconducting qubits with a tunable broadband Purcell filter

summary.summary: A shared $\Pi$-shaped Purcell filter integrated into the feedline provides broadband qubit protection in multiplexed circuit-QED via passive microwave interference between two open-ended stubs. For realistic parameters, the design achieves Purcell-limited relaxation times exceeding 1 ms over approximately 1.5 GHz while preserving dispersive readout.
summary.motivation: Existing Purcell filters either require per-channel implementations (increasing overhead with processor size) or higher-order designs with multiple resonant sections (added complexity). A simple, shared filter that suppresses $\Re\{Y_\mathrm{env}(\omega)\}$ across the qubit band without degrading readout would enable scalable multiplexed architectures.
summary.method: Two open-ended transmission-line stubs of lengths $\ell_+$ and $\ell_-$ are connected by an in-line section of length $\ell \approx (\ell_+ + \ell_-)/2$, forming a $\Pi$ network. The stubs' resonances at $\omega_\pm = \pi v/(2\ell_\pm)$ create overlapping suppression windows; destructive interference in the reflected field (setting $1 + L_1(\omega) \approx 0$ in the scattering picture) cancels radiative coupling to the external environment. SPICE and finite-element (HFSS) simulations verify performance for transmon-based architectures.
summary.result: Simulations with realistic circuit parameters ($C_q = 81$ fF, $C_\mathrm{out} = 110$ fF, stub lengths $\ell_+ = 6.73$ mm and $\ell_- = 7.38$ mm) yield $T_P > 1$ ms over the target band [4.2, 4.5] GHz; four simultaneous qubits in a multiplexed readout architecture each achieve protection exceeding 1 ms within a 1.5 GHz window. Readout-mode frequency shift remains below 1 MHz, preserving compatibility with dispersive measurement.

papers.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Hybrid Electro- and Opto-mechanical system coupled to Superconducting Qubit: A Short Review
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubits, realized by incorporating Josephson junctions into superconducting circuits, behave as artificial atoms with anharmonic energy spectra and can be precisely controlled and measured using microwave cavities within the framework of circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED). Since its emergence in the early 2000s, cQED has established superconducting qubits as leading candidates for scalable quantum devices and has enabled the exploration of hybrid quantum systems that integrate disparate physical platformsThis review surveys superconducting hybrid quantum electromechanical systems in which mechanical resonators are coupled to superconducting qubits, with a focus on two widely used qubit platforms: the transmon and the fluxonium. We provide an overview of the underlying coupling mechanisms arising from interactions through the phase and charge degrees of freedom of the qubit, and discuss how these mechanisms give rise to both longitudinal and transverse qubit-mechanical interactions. We further review extensions of electromechanical platforms to electro-optomechanical architectures, in which optical cavities are integrated to enable coherent interfacing between superconducting circuits and optical photons. This review aims to present a unified framework and perspective on qubit-mechanical and qubit-mechanical-optical hybrid systems in superconducting quantum technologies and applications related to sensors.

similar_to.title: Circuit Quantum Electrodynamics: Coherent Coupling of a Single Photon to a Cooper Pair Box

summary.summary: This review comprehensively covers superconducting hybrid quantum electromechanical and electro-optomechanical systems, focusing on transmon and fluxonium qubits coupled to mechanical resonators through charge and phase degrees of freedom. The paper discusses coupling mechanisms, coherent interactions, and applications including ground-state cooling, quantum state transfer, entanglement generation, and quantum sensing using these integrated platforms.
summary.motivation: Hybrid superconducting quantum systems combining disparate physical platforms enable novel quantum phenomena and sensing capabilities by leveraging the complementary strengths of circuit QED with mechanical and optical resonators, providing pathways toward scalable quantum technologies and quantum networks.
summary.method: The review presents a unified theoretical framework starting from basic concepts (two-level systems, harmonic oscillators, superconductivity), then details Cooper pair box implementations (charge, transmon, fluxonium qubits), their dispersive readout via microwave cavities, and derives effective Hamiltonians for qubit-mechanical coupling via charge ($g_{T/F} = 4E_C^{T/F} C_m^{T/F} x_0 / \hbar e$) and phase ($g_{Tm} = \alpha x_0 \sin(\pi\Phi_e/\Phi_0)/\hbar$) degrees of freedom, extending to optomechanical architectures.
summary.result: The framework enables quantum phenomena including vacuum Rabi oscillations with $\Omega_n = \sqrt{G^2(n+1) + (\Delta/2)^2}$, ground-state cooling via red-detuned drives, generation of entangled states and cat states in mechanical modes, phonon-number-resolved spectroscopy with spectral shifts $\chi \propto G^2/\delta$, and quantum transduction between microwave and optical domains via coherent state transfer protocols.

papers.title: Numerical simulation methods for quantum sensing at parametric criticality
papers.abstract: Microwave photon detection is a key technology for low-temperature superconducting electronics and quantum information processing. A promising possibility is to use switching processes in parametric superconducting devices at criticality, which can be triggered by small perturbations. Here we demonstrate the unique sensing properties of the superconducting Kerr parametric resonator when operated in the proximity of the phase transition boundary. We utilize a semiclassical approximation to provide numerical and analytical results for the Heisenberg-Langevin and Fokker-Planck equations that describe the switching mechanism. We show that the probability of switching events is enhanced by probe input states with energies down to single quanta levels.

summary.summary: This work develops numerical simulation methods for microwave photon detection using superconducting Kerr parametric resonators operated near the parametric instability threshold. The authors solve Heisenberg-Langevin and Fokker-Planck equations in a semiclassical approximation to characterize switching dynamics and show that detection efficiency is enhanced by probe signals down to single-photon levels.
summary.motivation: Parametric devices at criticality exhibit heightened sensitivity to weak perturbations, offering a promising avenue for single-photon detection in superconducting quantum systems. Understanding the switching mechanisms and detection performance near the phase transition boundary is essential for practical implementations in quantum information processing.
summary.method: Semiclassical treatment of a parametrically pumped Kerr oscillator via Heisenberg-Langevin equations, using separation of slow and fast quadratures to derive an effective potential analogous to Landau free energy in phase transitions. Fokker-Planck equation solved numerically and analytically to compute switching probabilities and detection efficiency for coherent probe states.
summary.result: At operational point with $|\alpha|/(\kappa+\gamma)=0.506$, $\Delta/(2\pi)=0.748$ MHz, $K/(\kappa+\gamma)=-3.12\times10^{-5}$: dark count probability $p_{\text{dark}}\approx0.14$, single-photon switching probability $P_{1^+}\approx0.52$, and detection efficiency $\eta\approx0.58$ for $n̄=1$ photon pulses; analytical solutions for Kerr-free resonators ($K=0$) confirm the approximations.
